newsitem.title: USA: California judge orders Jewish charity closed.
newsitem.headline: California judge orders Jewish charity closed.

text.p: A California judge on Tuesday ordered the liquidation of the assets of a controversial charity set up to help Russian Jewish immigrants in the United States.

Judge William Cahill of the San Francisco Superior Court ordered a receiver to close all the businesses of the Jewish Educational Centre, liquidate all its assets "as soon as practicable" and fire all its employees.
The written order was sought by the California attorney general's office, which filed a civil suit against the San Francisco-based charity last month alleging diversion of assets.

The centre was set up to help Russian Jewish immigrants who settled in the United States. It advertised heavily in northern California for donations of old cars that it sold at auction, becoming one of the nation's largest used-car operations and raising millions of dollars a year.
The court appointed a receiver to take control of the nonprofit organisation last month after the state attorney general and the San Francisco district attorney each filed civil actions against it.

The district attorney's office accused officials of the charity of false advertising and unfair business practices. It said that while the group's advertising said 100 percent of donations went to charity, only about 20 percent did.
Court-appointed receiver David Bradlow has said the charity had $150,000 in the bank and $500,000 in bills.

California Deputy Attorney General Belinda Johns said she was pleased with the judge's decision. "I think now the receiver can get on with the business of winding up, which became clearly necessary after we saw the state of the JEC's finances," she said.

Carol Ruth Silver, recently appointed chairwoman of the center's board of directors, said it had had problems with accounting because it grew so rapidly. She said its fund-raising costs were no worse than those of many other organisations.
